policy.originality: Official materials may define structures, skills, scoring models, aggregate statistics, passage specifications, and rubric dimensions. Scholark does not republish, number-swap, or closely paraphrase copyrighted questions.
policy.scoring: Published models and aggregate statistics provide independent priors. Scholark score ranges remain estimates because operational item parameters are not public.
policy.updates: Every source has a review date. A release audit fails when a required source becomes stale or its URL is missing.

sources.title: Digital SAT Suite of Assessments Technical Manual
sources.contentPolicy: Specifications and aggregate methodology only; do not reproduce operational or sample items.

sources.title: Digital SAT Suite Content Domains and Assessment Framework
sources.contentPolicy: Use taxonomy and specifications; write independent passages, contexts, stems, and distractors.

sources.title: How Digital SAT Scores Are Calculated
sources.contentPolicy: Use public score interpretation; never claim access to College Board operational scoring.

sources.title: SAT Nationally Representative and User Percentiles
sources.contentPolicy: Use published aggregate percentile ranks with attribution; do not imply Scholark caused an outcome.

sources.title: SAT Suite of Assessments Program Results 2025
sources.contentPolicy: Use aggregate participation statistics with year and publisher attribution.

sources.title: Design Framework for the ACT Enhancements
sources.contentPolicy: Use blueprint and research findings; do not reproduce study forms or copyrighted items.

sources.title: Interpreting Scores on the Enhanced ACT
sources.contentPolicy: Use public aggregate findings and score meaning; do not imply official equating.

sources.title: ACT-tested Class of 2025 Graduating Class Data
sources.contentPolicy: Use aggregate national statistics with attribution; never attribute the published retesting gain to Scholark.

sources.title: Commas vs. Semicolons in Compound Sentences
sources.contentPolicy: Teach the underlying grammar rule in original language and link the source; do not copy examples.

sources.title: Past AP Free-Response Questions and Scoring Information
sources.contentPolicy: Reserved for the later AP phase. Link to released prompts; create original practice instead of republishing banks.
